text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Three Israeli soldiers killed in Lebanon.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: Syria must restrain Hizbollah guerrillas in Lebanon.
- Government will order Bank Discount to sell off Mercantile Discount Bank during the year, says general manager of MI Holdings, the state-owned company in charge of bank sales.
- Israeli consulates in San Francisco, Philadelphia may be closed in money-saving move.
- Israel Electric Corp workers gear up to fight government decision to reduce company franchise from 10 years to six.
- Histadrut trade unions federation bank workers to meet on Sunday to decide whether to shift from six- to five-day work week.

- In secret letter from ex-U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher to Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, the United States promised to carry out the Hebron agreement and there's no contradiction in the letter sent to Netanyahu.
- Police investigator says there has been progress in investigation of the attorney-general affair and there's certainly a point to continuing it.
- Netanyahu demands of Syrian President Hafez al-Assad: Stop the slaughter in Lebanon.
- Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai: The attack in Lebanon could influence the peace process.
- Netanyahu's political adviser Dore Gold returns from secret mission. Effort to improve ties with Morocco, Gulf states.
